SMTO-EXE-0150 — SMTO can't type into password fields for you

GUID: 5037424f-1ed6-5823-8bb4-5589263574d2
Slug: ui-secret-binding-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO was about to type into a password field, and it never does that, to keep your secrets out of its records. Nothing was typed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer), click the password field in the app and type the password yourself. SMTO deliberately never types passwords, so this part has to be done by you.
  2. When SMTO asks, reply that you've entered it. Don't type the password into the SMTO conversation. SMTO only needs to know the step is done; your password stays private.

What success looks like

  • The app accepts the password, and SMTO continues with the next step of the task.

If it still fails

  • If you can't reach that computer to type the password, tell SMTO you can't, and ask the person who manages that computer to sign in for you. Never share the password in the conversation or in error reports.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Set-value, typing or key input targeted a secure/password control, and the UI capability has no approved private secret-binding route.

What this means

  • Set-value, typing or key input targeted a secure/password control, for which this UI capability has no approved private secret-binding route. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Set-value, typing or key input targeted a secure/password control, for which this UI capability has no approved private secret-binding route.

How to diagnose it

  • Confirm the target's secure classification and keep credential contents out of tool arguments and diagnostic evidence.

How to fix it

  • Use the ask_user checkpoint to have the user enter the credential directly in the target application, then confirm completion without disclosing it. Never pass passwords in ui.* tool arguments; ui.set_value, ui.type_text and ui.key_press reject secure fields and no set_secret tool exists.
  • Ask the user to enter credentials directly in the target application and confirm completion through ask_user. Do not supply passwords in tool arguments.

Retry and execution caution

  • Ask the user to enter credentials directly in the target application and confirm completion through ask_user. Do not supply passwords in tool arguments.

How to verify the fix

  • The user completes the private credential step in the intended application and confirms completion without disclosing the secret.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
